headline: NO FULL-CONTEXT MEASUREMENT EXISTS. All three runs were quote-only: the abstract lookup failed silently twice (checkpoint keys are marker-stripped and further normalized; prefix matching against the raw corpus returned null on all 20 rows both times, falling back to the quote). What the three runs DO establish: the gate killed 4/17, 8/17 and 10/17 true positives and at most 1/3 false ones, never raising precision. Runs 2 and 3 sent BYTE-IDENTICAL prompts and killed 8 vs 10 — the provider is not deterministic at temperature 0, which independently undermines a gate whose verdict flips run to run.

run2.note: verbatim prompt, quote-only (lookup silently null on 20/20)

run3.note: identical prompts to run2 after a failed lookup fix — 8 vs 10 on the same bytes is provider nondeterminism

correction: Commit 595130e cited run 2 as full-context; that was wrong, caught by the 2026-08-22 accuracy review and by full_abstract:false on every row. The removal decision SURVIVES: every measurement at every attempted context level kills mostly true positives, and the verdict is not even stable across identical inputs. A faithful full-abstract run remains OPEN and needs the lookup keyed by the fired row's evidence doc_id, not by claim-prefix matching.
